newsitem.title: USA: Argentine minister sees IMF loan by September.
newsitem.headline: Argentine minister sees IMF loan by September.

text.p: A loan agreement between Argentina and the International Monetary Fund is likely to be in place in September, Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said on Tuesday.

Fernandez, who met with IMF officials in Washington, told reporters that the loan would probably be for about $1 billion. "We have advanced enough to be confident that we will announce an agreement in Hong Kong," he said. The IMF annual meeting takes place in Hong Kong in the second half of September.
Fernandez had said on Friday that the deal could be delayed.
But after meeting with IMF officials and lunching with IMF managing director Michel Camdessus on Tuesday, he said he was confident a basic agreement would be in place by September.
The EFF would replace Argentina's current stand-by program, which expires at the end of this year.
Fernandez said Argentina was still negotiating with the IMF over how to reduce its current federal and provincial deficits over the next two years.

"The main requirement continues to be the fiscal solvency of the Argentine state," Fernandez told a news conference. "What we are negotiating now is a gradual reduction in the deficit up to the year 2000."
By the IMF meeting in Hong Kong there will be agreement on the fiscal projections for 1998 and 1999, he said.
Fernandez denied reports that the IMF was worried about Argentina's deficit getting out of hand.
"We are still on track with this target of $4.5 billion for 1997," he said. "Our public accounts are under control."
